subject: physics
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: How are the particles arranged in a solid according to the kinetic particle model?
options: Closely packed in a regular pattern, vibrating about fixed positions
Far apart and moving randomly at high speed
Close together but able to slide past one another
Widely spaced in a fixed regular lattice with no motion
questions.explain: In a solid the particles are held in a fixed, regular lattice and can only vibrate about their fixed positions.

questions.q: The random, jerky motion of smoke particles seen through a microscope is called:
questions.explain: Brownian motion is the random movement of small particles caused by collisions with fast-moving, invisible air molecules.

questions.q: The pressure a gas exerts on the walls of its container is caused by:
options: Gas molecules colliding with the walls
The weight of the gas molecules
Attraction between the molecules and the walls
questions.explain: Gas pressure results from the many collisions of moving molecules with the container walls.

questions.q: Which group of materials are generally the best conductors of thermal energy?
questions.explain: Metals conduct thermal energy well because they contain free (delocalised) electrons that transfer energy quickly.

questions.q: Which type of surface is the best emitter of infrared radiation?
questions.explain: Dull, black surfaces are the best emitters (and absorbers) of infrared radiation, while shiny surfaces are poor emitters.

questions.q: What is the correct SI-based unit for specific heat capacity?
questions.explain: Specific heat capacity is the energy per kilogram per degree Celsius, so its unit is J/(kg °C).

questions.q: For the same temperature rise, which state of matter generally expands the most?
questions.explain: Gases expand the most for a given temperature rise, solids the least, because gas particles are least strongly held.

questions.q: When a fixed mass of gas is heated at constant volume, its pressure increases because the molecules:
options: Move faster and hit the walls harder and more often
Grow larger and take up more space
Become heavier and press down more
Move closer together near the walls
questions.explain: Heating raises the molecules' average kinetic energy, so they collide with the walls harder and more frequently, raising the pressure.

questions.q: Why does a liquid cool down as it evaporates?
options: The faster, more energetic molecules escape, lowering the average energy of those left
Evaporation adds cold air to the liquid
The slowest molecules escape first, carrying away energy
Evaporation reduces the mass so temperature must fall
questions.explain: The most energetic molecules escape during evaporation, reducing the average kinetic energy, and hence temperature, of the remaining liquid.

questions.q: In convection, warm fluid rises because when it is heated it becomes:
options: Less dense than the surrounding cooler fluid
More dense than the surrounding cooler fluid
A better conductor than the cooler fluid
questions.explain: Heating a fluid makes it expand and become less dense, so it rises and cooler denser fluid sinks, setting up a convection current.

questions.q: Thermal radiation differs from conduction and convection because it:
options: Requires particles to carry the energy
questions.explain: Thermal radiation is electromagnetic (infrared) energy and needs no medium, so it can travel through a vacuum such as space.

questions.q: As the temperature of a gas rises, what happens to the average kinetic energy of its molecules?
questions.explain: The average kinetic energy of the molecules is directly related to the temperature, so it increases as temperature rises.

questions.q: For a fixed mass of gas at constant temperature, how does the pressure change if the volume is decreased?
options: Pressure increases, since pressure and volume are inversely proportional
Pressure decreases, since pressure and volume are directly proportional
questions.explain: At constant temperature pV is constant, so reducing the volume increases the pressure.

questions.q: Why are metals much better thermal conductors than non-metals?
options: They contain free electrons that transfer energy rapidly
questions.explain: Free (delocalised) electrons in metals move and transfer thermal energy quickly, in addition to lattice vibrations.
